trip.title: Grand Mediterranean Luxury Guide
trip.subtitle: Four Seasons I · Western Mediterranean
trip.route: Málaga → Menorca → La Joliette → Saint-Tropez → Ponza → Trapani → Gozo → Valletta

connecting.baggage: Hand baggage: 2 pieces per person, Hold: 1 piece per person
connecting.notes: Free day in Amsterdam on Mar 18. Hotel: The Dylan Amsterdam (booked).

days.label: Pre-Cruise: Outbound Flights (Legs 1–2)
days.description: SMF → SEA → AMS. Depart Sacramento 11:35 AM, arrive Amsterdam 10:00 AM (+1 day). Delta First Class, confirmation GEVMLH.

days.label: Pre-Cruise: Amsterdam Layover
days.description: Arrive AMS 10:00 AM. Check-in at The Dylan Amsterdam at 3:00 PM (early check-in requested). Rijksmuseum guided tour at 1:00 PM. Dinner at De Silveren Spiegel at 6:30 PM.

hotel.name: The Dylan Amsterdam
hotel.earlyCheckIn: Requested — confirmation will be emailed to robert.lambert@gmail.com
hotel.luggageNote: If early check-in unavailable: hotel will stow luggage. Freshen up in bathrooms (gym does not have showers).

excursions.name: Rijksmuseum Amsterdam Semi-Private Guided Tour
excursions.notes: Semi-private guided tour. Card ending 1004 auto-charged $144.50 on 03/16/26. Mobile ticket accepted — print or save to phone. Tour operator: Rijksmuseum Tours, Nachtwachtlaan 204, Amsterdam. Operator phone: +31655551914.

dining.name: De Silveren Spiegel
dining.notes: 7-course tasting menu. Deposit: €50 (charged to credit card). Confirmation sent to raelanmrlambert@gmail.com. ALLERGY NOTE: Raelan is intolerant to fresh garlic — restaurant has been notified. Cancellation policy: 24 hours in advance or full menu price charged. Smart casual dress code. Allow ~3.5 hours for the experience.

recommendations.name: Canal District Walk
recommendations.description: Stroll the UNESCO-listed canal ring; stop at Café 't Smalle for traditional Dutch atmosphere

days.label: Pre-Cruise: Amsterdam → Málaga
days.description: Vueling IB5689 — AMS 11:40 AM → AGP 2:50 PM (3h 10m). Economy class, confirmation K60WW. Transfer to Hotel Vincci Selección Posada del Patio upon arrival in Málaga.

hotel.name: Hotel Vincci Selección Posada del Patio
hotel.room: Vincci Essence Triple Superior — 5-star hotel in Málaga's historic center
hotel.cancellation: Free cancellation until March 18, 2026. From March 18 at 2:00 PM: full stay charged (€461.99). Payment at hotel.

dining.name: Bodegas El Pimpi
dining.notes: Walk-in — expect ~20-minute wait. Online reservations not available. Iconic Málaga wine bar adjacent to the Alcazaba. Excellent sherries, tapas, and fritura malagueña.

recommendations.name: Málaga Historic Center
recommendations.description: Explore the cathedral and Picasso Museum if arriving with time to spare

recommendations.name: Bodegas El Pimpi (PLANNED — walk-in dinner)
recommendations.description: Iconic Málaga wine bar adjacent to the Alcazaba, Calle Granada 62. Walk-in only — no online reservations. Expect ~20-minute wait. Sherries from the barrel, tapas, fritura malagueña. The definitive Málaga evening.

excursions.name: Hammam Al Ándalus — MIMMA60 Ritual
excursions.address: C/ Plaza de los Mártires, 5, Málaga
excursions.notes: 2x MIMMA60 y bruma perfumada de El Jardín del Hammam. 60-minute bath ritual with perfumed mist experience. Total: €278.00.

dining.name: Cambara at Muelle Uno
dining.notes: Post-Hammam lunch (~12:30 PM finish → walk to port). Mediterranean/fusion, rice dishes, harbor terrace. Right at the port — zero transit stress before 4:00 PM boarding. ~€20–30/person. Walk-in friendly.

dining.name: Dinner on the yacht
dining.notes: Eating onboard for first evening — explore the ship's restaurants. Note: dinner is pay-as-you-go (only breakfast at Terrasse is complimentary).

recommendations.name: Blossom (1 Michelin Star)
recommendations.description: Chef Emi Schobert's modern fusion on the 4th floor of Palacio de la Aduana — terrace overlooks the Alcazaba. 9-course 'Esencia' or 15-course 'Confluencia' tasting menus. Only 8 tables. The most exciting new restaurant in Málaga.

recommendations.name: Kaleja (1 Michelin Star)
recommendations.description: Chef Dani Carnero's 'cocina de candela' — ember and wood-fired cooking reviving Andalusian traditions with modern technique. Hidden in the old Jewish quarter. ~16-course tasting menu.

recommendations.name: Palodu (1 Michelin Star, new 2026)
recommendations.description: Chefs Cristina Cánovas & Diego Aguilar's 'dual cuisine' concept — both chefs must approve every dish. Steps from Atarazanas Market. Lunch seating 1:30–2:30 PM. Closed Sun/Mon.

recommendations.name: José Carlos García (1 Michelin Star)
recommendations.description: 10 consecutive years starred. Two tasting menus: standard (~€160) or JCG Menu (~€236). Located at Muelle Uno, directly on the port — walk to boarding after lunch. Glass-and-steel design with vertical garden.

recommendations.name: Centre Pompidou Málaga
recommendations.description: The Centre Pompidou's first international outpost, housed in Daniel Buren's multicolored glass cube on the port. Works by Picasso, Miró, Bacon, Magritte, and Frida Kahlo. Right at Muelle Uno — combine with José Carlos García.

recommendations.name: Hammam Al Ándalus (BOOKED — 10:00 AM)
recommendations.description: BOOKED: MIMMA60 ritual at 10:00 AM. Luxury Arab baths in the historic center inspired by Málaga's Moorish heritage. Hot, warm, and cold thermal pools, steam room, and perfumed mist experience. Booking #419456.

recommendations.name: Alcazaba & Gibralfaro Castle
recommendations.description: 11th-century Moorish fortress with panoramic port views. Allow 1.5–2 hours; it's uphill. Best as a morning activity before lunch — choose this or Picasso Museum, not both, given boarding deadline.

recommendations.name: Museo Picasso Málaga & Casa Natal
recommendations.description: Over 285 works in the Buenavista Palace, plus Picasso's birthplace at Plaza de la Merced. Consider a private guided Picasso walk connecting both sites.

recommendations.name: Atarazanas Market
recommendations.description: Historic 19th-century iron-and-glass market for fresh seafood, olives, and local produce. Perfect for morning grazing before a Michelin lunch.

gaps.description: Hammam 10:00 AM → Cambara lunch ~1:00 PM → boarding by 4:00 PM. Consider Centre Pompidou or Muelle Uno stroll between lunch and boarding.

recommendations.name: Spa & Wellness
recommendations.description: Full-service spa aboard the Four Seasons I — book treatments early

recommendations.name: Pool Deck
recommendations.description: Relax on the sun deck; the yacht's intimate size means no crowds

excursions.name: Subaida Farm — Guided Tour & Cheese Tasting
excursions.notes: CONFIRMED: Subaida Farm (Alaior), 2 guests, 11:30 AM – 1:00 PM guided tour + cheese tasting. D.O.P. certified, 350-hectare estate, 3 generations of cheesemaking. ~20–30 min drive from Mahón port. Includes cheese & sausage tasting. After tour: drive back to Mahón, lunch aboard yacht at Terrasse, board by 3 PM.

optionA.name: Quesos Sa Roqueta (Ferreries)
optionA.type: Hands-on cheesemaking + farm tour + tasting (2.5 hrs, max 6 people)
optionA.highlights: Make your own Mahón cheese, feed cows/calves, personalize a cheese shipped home after 8-week cure
optionA.booking: Contact farm directly (GetYourGuide sold out for 3/22)

optionB.name: Subaida Farm (Alaior)
optionB.type: Guided farm tour + Menorcan breakfast (1 hr)
optionB.highlights: D.O.P. certified, 350-hectare estate, 3 generations of cheesemaking, master cheesemaker demo, calf feeding, cheese & sausage tasting
optionB.location: Road from Alaior to Arenal d'en Castell

excursions.logistics: Car service: Zone Transfers — WhatsApp +34 654 381 547 (hours: 9:00–14:00 & 16:00–19:00), email info@zonetransfers.com. Route: Mahón port → Subaida Farm, Alaior (~20–30 min) → Mahón port. Need to contact to book.

recommendations.name: Talayotic Menorca UNESCO Sites
recommendations.description: 2023 UNESCO World Heritage inscription. ~1,600 prehistoric sites including mysterious taulas (T-shaped megaliths found nowhere else on Earth). Key sites: Naveta des Tudons (oldest roofed building in Europe), Torralba d'en Salort, Torre d'en Galmes. Private archaeologist-guided half-day tours available. Perfect for March — outdoor, year-round.

recommendations.name: Xoriguer Gin Distillery + Mahón Markets
recommendations.description: If time allows before farm visit: guided tour at Xoriguer (family-owned since 1784, 1 hr, €15/person, includes gin, pomada, and hierbas tastings paired with local cheese). Then walk to Mercat de Peix (century-old fish market with tapas bars). All year-round, near the port.

recommendations.name: Hauser & Wirth Gallery + Cantina on Illa del Rei
recommendations.description: World-class art gallery on a tiny island in Mahón harbor, occupying a restored 18th-century British naval hospital. Features a Piet Oudolf-designed garden (the High Line designer). Cantina restaurant serves Mediterranean plates in an olive grove with harbor views. Free ferry, free gallery entry. MUST CONFIRM MARCH OPENING — contact +34 871 18 38 45 or menorca@hauserwirth.com.

recommendations.name: Subaida Farm (BOOKED — 11:30 AM)
recommendations.description: BOOKED: 11:30 AM – 1:00 PM guided tour & cheese tasting at Subaida Farm, Alaior. D.O.P. certified estate, master cheesemaker demo, cheese & sausage tasting. After tour: drive back to Mahón, lunch aboard yacht at Terrasse, board by 3 PM.

recommendations.name: Es Tast de na Sílvia (Ciutadella)
recommendations.description: The only restaurant in the Balearics with both Slow Food and Km.0 certifications. Chef Sílvia shops the market daily; menu changes every day. Cash only. In Ciutadella (~45 min drive). Confirm March hours: +34 971 387 895.

recommendations.name: Cala Macarella (scenic hike only in March)
recommendations.description: One of the Mediterranean's most beautiful coves (30 min drive). Note: water is ~59°F in March and beach facilities are closed. Worth visiting as a scenic coastal hike, not a beach day.

gaps.description: Subaida Farm booked (11:30 AM – 1:00 PM). Car service identified: Zone Transfers (WhatsApp +34 654 381 547, info@zonetransfers.com) — still need to book.

recommendations.name: Morning: Le Panier Quarter + MuCEM
recommendations.description: Recommended morning plan. Walk Le Panier (Marseille's oldest neighborhood, 5 min from tender zone) — narrow streets, colorful façades, street art, artisan studios. Then MuCEM museum (open Mondays, closed Tuesdays). Walkable from La Joliette port. Allow 2–3 hours for both.

recommendations.name: Bouillant by Alexandre Mazzia (MuCEM rooftop) — PRIMARY LUNCH
recommendations.description: Alexandre Mazzia's casual bistro on the MuCEM rooftop (opened Sept 2025). His 3-star creative DNA in an accessible format — €18–24/dish, no reservations needed. Panoramic sea and cathedral views. Pairs perfectly with the museum visit. Open Monday lunch ~12:00–2:30 PM.

recommendations.name: Belle de Mars (1 Michelin Star, new 2025)
recommendations.description: The hottest new table in Marseille. Chefs Michel Marini & Kim-Mai Bui (Passédat alumni). Pretty, seasonal dishes of local seafood and vegetables. Near the Vieux-Port at 56 Rue de Forbin. OPEN MONDAY — tight lunch window 12:15–1:30 PM. Needs reservation NOW: +33 9 86 57 24 58.

recommendations.name: Chez Fonfon (Bib Gourmand)
recommendations.description: Iconic bouillabaisse since 1952 in the Vallon des Auffes — Marseille's tiny fisherman's harbor. ~€65/person for the full bouillabaisse (the reason to come). Must order 24 hours ahead: +33 4 91 52 14 38. Open Monday lunch 12:00–2:00 PM. 15 min taxi from port.

recommendations.name: Une Table au Sud (1 Michelin Star)
recommendations.description: Chef Ludovic Turac's Provençal-Armenian fusion directly overlooking the Vieux-Port with views to Notre-Dame de la Garde. Ideal setting for a yacht-day lunch. 2 Quai du Port.

recommendations.name: La Mercerie
recommendations.description: Not starred but editorially essential — named across Eater, Le Fooding, and The Infatuation. British chef Harry Cummins in a former haberdashery in Noailles. Seasonal, Mediterranean-inflected, ingredient-driven. 9 Cours Saint-Louis.

recommendations.name: Calanques National Park (Scenic Boat Tour)
recommendations.description: Dramatic limestone fjords — hire a private boat from the Vieux-Port. Operators like Bleu Évasion offer luxury charters with skipper, wine, and Provençal tapas. Scenic cruise only — water is ~14°C in March, no swimming. Beautiful from the boat.

recommendations.name: Château d'If — ⚠️ CLOSED MONDAYS (Oct–Mar)
recommendations.description: The island fortress that inspired Dumas's 'The Count of Monte Cristo.' CLOSED on Mondays in low season (Oct 1–Mar 31) — confirmed via chateau-if.fr. The Frioul Islands ferry still runs for scenery, but the castle itself is inaccessible March 23.

recommendations.name: Le Vieux-Port
recommendations.description: The historic Old Port — morning fish market, cafés, and the Norman Foster mirror canopy. Departure point for Calanques boats.

gaps.description: No formal excursion booked. Suggested plan: Le Panier + MuCEM morning → Bouillant lunch on MuCEM rooftop → return aboard for Sedna at 6 PM. Note: AM par Alexandre Mazzia and Le Petit Nice are both CLOSED Mondays. Château d'If also closed.

excursions.name: Golf Club Saint-Tropez
excursions.notes: 18-hole round at one of the Riviera's premier courses. Includes transfers.

dining.name: Le Café (Saint-Tropez)
dining.notes: PENDING — reservation request submitted via SevenRooms for Raelan Lambert, Tuesday March 24, 7:30 PM, 2 guests. Restaurant has 19 days to respond. No phone call needed. Iconic Place des Lices restaurant.

recommendations.name: Musée de l'Annonciade
recommendations.description: Exceptional post-Impressionist and Fauvist art in a converted 16th-century chapel. Signac, Matisse, Bonnard. Small enough to see in 45 minutes.

recommendations.name: Place des Lices Market — IT'S TUESDAY!
recommendations.description: The town's famous Provençal market runs Tuesdays & Saturdays — you're here on a Tuesday. Lavender, olive oils, produce, antiques. Arrives early morning, winds down by ~1 PM. Don't miss it.

recommendations.name: Colette at Hotel Sezz (1 Michelin Star)
recommendations.description: Evening dinner alternative if Le Café falls through. Elegant Mediterranean cuisine at the design-forward Hotel Sezz. Call to verify Tuesday opening: +33 (0)4 94 44 53 11.

recommendations.name: Au Caprice des Deux
recommendations.description: Provençal bistro since 1994, romantic setting. Solid fallback dinner option. Confirm Tuesday hours: +33 (0)4 94 97 76 78.

gaps.description: Le Café reservation request submitted (7:30 PM, 2 guests) — awaiting restaurant confirmation via SevenRooms.

recommendations.name: Recovery Day
recommendations.description: Rest and recharge after Saint-Tropez. Spa, pool, or catch up on reading.

excursions.name: A Day on Ponza Island (Four Seasons Excursion)
excursions.notes: Four Seasons shore excursion: explore Ponza's port and ancient streets, Michelin-star lunch with sea views, visit iconic Chiaia di Luna beach. $2,945/guest. All ages. Need to reserve.

recommendations.name: Private Boat Circumnavigation of Ponza
recommendations.description: The single best thing to do on Ponza. Key stops: Grotte di Pilato (2,000-year-old Roman fish farm), Punta di Capo Bianco (extraordinary blue light at midday), Grotta della Maga Circe, Cala del Core (heart-shaped cliff scar), Le Formiche (crystal-clear visibility). Allow 4–5 hours with stops. Can extend to Palmarola Island. OPERATORS: (1) Cooperativa Barcaioli Ponzesi — the island's main boat cooperative. Off-season contact: Fabio Conte +39 340 397 9916, info@barcaioliponza.it, barcaioliponza.it. (2) ZioJack Ponza — private charter specialist, vessel 'Carmine' (up to 7 guests). +39 349 556 0424, ziojackponza@gmail.com. (3) Ciccio Nero Nautica — 40+ years, motorboat rentals + guided tours. +39 0771 80697, isolaponza.it. (4) SamBoat platform (samboat.com) as online fallback. Also: Four Seasons concierge may arrange through local contacts — worth asking.

recommendations.name: Palmarola Island
recommendations.description: Uninhabited island 30 min west of Ponza — described by Condé Nast Traveler as 'one of the most beautiful islands in the Mediterranean.' Dramatic Faraglioni di San Silverio rock formations. In March you'll have it essentially to yourselves.

recommendations.name: Grotte di Pilato (Roman Grottoes)
recommendations.description: Five interconnected rock-cut basins from the 1st century CE — an elaborate Roman moray eel farm connected to Augustus's imperial villa above. Archaeological finds include a marble statue (discovered 1997). Accessible by boat near the port. Genuinely unique.

recommendations.name: Acqua Pazza (1 Michelin Star)
recommendations.description: Luigi Pesce's celebrated seafood with 20+ consecutive years starred. Multi-tiered terraces with panoramic port views — 'one of the most spectacular views in Italy.' Begin with the raw seafood crudi selection. MUST CONFIRM MARCH HOURS: +39 0771 80643. March is off-season.

recommendations.name: Il Tramonto
recommendations.description: Perched high above the sea with the best views on Ponza, looking out to Palmarola. Refined seafood — the paccheri with prawns is phenomenal. Finish with a chilled glass of finocchietto (wild fennel liqueur, a Ponza specialty). Confirm March availability.

recommendations.name: Biancolella di Ponza Wine
recommendations.description: One of Italy's rarest wines (~1,500 bottles/year) from Antiche Cantine Migliaccio. Made from vines brought to Ponza in 1734, grown on volcanic tuff soil reachable only by swimming or a 40-min hike. Intensely mineral with citrus notes. Order at any restaurant.

recommendations.name: Natural Pools of Cala Feola
recommendations.description: Beautiful natural rock pools on the western coast. Note: beach facilities closed in March. Best visited as a stop on the boat tour rather than a land-based excursion.

recommendations.name: Chiaia di Luna Viewpoint
recommendations.description: The beach itself is permanently closed due to fatal rockfalls from the unstable cliffs. However, the clifftop overlook offers a dramatic view of the crescent beach and towering white tuff cliffs. Brief stop during a port village walk.

gaps.description: No excursion booked yet. Four Seasons 'A Day on Ponza Island' available ($2,945/guest, 5 hrs) — or arrange private boat + Acqua Pazza independently. March is off-season — confirm restaurant availability in advance.

excursions.name: Ancient Ruins & Authentic Flavours
excursions.notes: Visit the Valley of the Temples–era ruins near Segesta, followed by a Sicilian food experience. Four Seasons excursion.

days.anniversary: 22nd wedding anniversary — ask Four Seasons concierge to arrange a special anniversary dinner onboard: private table, champagne, anniversary touches.

recommendations.name: Erice — Afternoon After Excursion (RECOMMENDED)
recommendations.description: Medieval hilltop village, the afternoon highlight. Timeline: 2:30 PM excursion ends → taxi to cable car station (~€10, 10 min) → Funivia di Erice cable car (Via Capua, Trapani → Erice in 10 min, €11 round trip, buy online at funiviaerice.skiperformance.com) → 3:00–4:30 PM in Erice → 4:45 PM back in Trapani → aboard by 5:30 PM (buffer before 6 PM departure). ⚠️ Verify March 27 cable car hours — seasonal transition is March 28: funiviaerice.it.

recommendations.name: Maria Grammatico Pasticceria (Erice)
recommendations.description: Sicily's most legendary pastry shop. Cassatelle (ricotta-filled fried pastries), genovesi (custard-filled shortcrust), cannoli. Maria Grammatico learned her craft from cloistered nuns as a girl. Via Vittorio Emanuele 14, Erice. Open daily 7 AM–10 PM.

recommendations.name: Castello di Venere (Norman Castle, Erice)
recommendations.description: 12th-century Norman fortress at the summit of Erice with panoramic views to the Egadi Islands and across western Sicily. Quick 15-min visit, combines with the pastry stop.

recommendations.name: Saline di Trapani
recommendations.description: Salt flats and windmills along the coast — particularly stunning at sunset. If skipping Erice, this is the alternative afternoon option.

recommendations.name: La Bettolaccia
recommendations.description: Outstanding Trapanese couscous (the local signature dish) in the historic center. If you're hungry after Erice.

recommendations.name: Anniversary Dinner Onboard 🥂
recommendations.description: 22nd wedding anniversary. Ask Four Seasons concierge to arrange: private table, champagne, anniversary touches. Erice is for the afternoon experience (Maria Grammatico pastries + prosecco with hilltop views), dinner is back aboard the yacht.

gaps.description: Afternoon plan: Erice via cable car after excursion (2:30–4:30 PM). Verify cable car hours for March 27 (seasonal transition March 28). Anniversary dinner onboard — contact concierge to arrange.

excursions.name: Guided Dive — Gozo
excursions.notes: Morning dive excursion off Gozo. Gozo is considered one of the Mediterranean's top dive destinations.

dining.name: Under Grain (1 Michelin Star)
dining.address: Beneath the Rosselli hotel, Merchants Street, Valletta
dining.notes: CONFIRMED via Tableo. Raelan Lambert, Saturday March 28, 7:00 PM, 2 adults, indoor seating. Comment on booking: '22 year wedding anniversary.' Vaulted 17th-century stone cellars. Seven consecutive years Michelin-starred. Cancellation: 24-hour notice required, €50/person penalty.

recommendations.name: Under Grain (BOOKED — 7:00 PM)
recommendations.description: BOOKED: 7:00 PM, 2 guests, confirmation 2JG-Z1M. Atmospheric vaulted stone ceilings in a 17th-century cellar beneath the Rosselli hotel. Seven consecutive years starred. Bold combinations — mussels with sweet Gorgonzola, Châteaubriand with mushroom variations. Anniversary dinner (22 years).

recommendations.name: Noni (1 Michelin Star)
recommendations.description: Chef Jonathan Brincat's 'playful and unstuffy' modern Maltese cuisine in a converted 17th-century townhouse. Standout deconstructed prawn cocktail. Alternative if Under Grain plans change.

recommendations.name: Trabuxu Wine Bar
recommendations.description: Valletta's first wine bar, set in a 400-year-old stone cellar on Strait Street. Over 20 years running. Exceptional wine list (Maltese, European, New World), artisan cheese and charcuterie. Perfect pre-dinner drinks before Under Grain.

recommendations.name: Upper Barrakka Gardens
recommendations.description: Stunning views of the Grand Harbour and the Three Cities. Don't miss the daily cannon-firing ceremony (noon and 4:00 PM). Free, iconic, essential Valletta.

recommendations.name: St. John's Co-Cathedral
recommendations.description: One of Europe's most important Baroque churches. Houses Caravaggio's 'Beheading of Saint John the Baptist' — his largest painting and the only one he signed.

recommendations.name: The Three Cities (by water taxi)
recommendations.description: Birgu, Senglea, and Cospicua — across the Grand Harbour by a 5-minute water taxi. Fort St. Angelo (the fortress that held during the Great Siege of 1565), narrow medieval streets, far fewer tourists than Valletta.

days.label: Disembarkation & Malta
days.description: Disembark Four Seasons I between 8:00–10:30 AM. Full day to explore Valletta. Overnight at The Phoenicia Malta. Early flight the next morning (6:00 AM MLA→CDG) — get to airport by 4:00 AM.

hotel.name: The Phoenicia Malta
hotel.chiefHost: Jovana Novakovic — jovana.novakovic@phoeniciamalta.com, +356 22911000, WhatsApp +35679220004 (available before/during/after stay). Requested: advise estimated arrival time.
hotel.room: Pegasus Suite — Art Deco design, king bed, separate living room, 441 ft². Fully stocked minibar, espresso machine, bathtub + separate shower.
hotel.includes: Daily breakfast at Contessa (main restaurant), early check-in/out (subject to availability), free Wi-Fi, free cancellation up to 3 days prior
hotel.spa: Phoenicia Spa & Wellness available until checkout. Bookings: spa@phoeniciamalta.com

recommendations.name: Upper Barrakka Gardens (morning)
recommendations.description: 5-min walk from The Phoenicia. Panoramic Grand Harbour views, noon cannon ceremony. Free. Perfect way to start the day after disembarkation.

recommendations.name: Caffè Cordina (morning coffee)
recommendations.description: Republic Street, founded 1837. Coffee, pastries, light lunch under painted ceilings. The most civilized way to pass time before hotel check-in. Iconic Valletta institution.

recommendations.name: St. John's Co-Cathedral
recommendations.description: Caravaggio's largest painting ('Beheading of Saint John the Baptist'), ornate Baroque interior, 45–60 min. ~€15/person. Book tickets: sjccocathedral.com.

recommendations.name: The Phoenicia Spa (afternoon)
recommendations.description: Leave bags with concierge after disembark, check in at 3 PM, book spa treatments for afternoon. Phone: +356 2291 1131.

recommendations.name: Mdina (The Silent City)
recommendations.description: Malta's former capital — a tiny walled hilltop city with fewer than 250 residents and 4,000 years of history. Honey-colored limestone alleys, Baroque palaces, quiet courtyards. Stop at Fontanella Tea Garden for coffee with sweeping countryside views. 25 min by car from Valletta.

recommendations.name: MICAS (Malta International Contemporary Art Space)
recommendations.description: 16,000 sq ft contemporary art gallery just outside Valletta. Designed by IPO Studio (Florence). Rooftop sculpture garden with commissions by Michele Oka Doner and Cristina Iglesias. Highlighted by Robb Report.

recommendations.name: ION Harbour by Simon Rogan (2 Michelin Stars) — SUNDAY DINNER
recommendations.description: ⚠️ March 29 is a Sunday. Rubino (Bib Gourmand) and Guzé Bistro (1★) are both CLOSED Sundays. ION Harbour is the quality option — hotel restaurant, likely open Sunday. Call: +356 9911 0166. Book 6:00–6:30 PM (need to be in bed by ~9:30 PM for 4:00 AM airport departure).

recommendations.name: The Phoenix (at The Phoenicia hotel)
recommendations.description: Fallback dinner option — ask concierge about Sunday dinner service. Convenient since you're staying at the hotel. Early seating recommended (~6:00 PM).

gaps.description: No dinner booked for Sunday evening. ION Harbour (2★) is the best Sunday option — call +356 9911 0166 for 6:00–6:30 PM. Need early dinner: 4:00 AM airport departure next morning.

days.label: Return Flights
days.description: MLA → CDG → LAX → SMF. Depart Malta 6:00 AM, arrive Sacramento 11:08 PM same day. Total duration: 26h 8m. Delta First Class, confirmation GEVMLH.

excursions.item: Hammam Al Ándalus — MIMMA60 Ritual, Málaga (Mar 20)

excursions.notes: Estimated ~€120–150 for two (tasting menu). Using €150 midpoint. USD estimate at ~$1.08/EUR.

expenses.totalExcursionsNote: Includes ~$300 USD estimate for Hammam Al Ándalus (€278 EUR) and ~$162 USD estimate for Under Grain dinner (€150 EUR). All other amounts in USD.
expenses.notes: Delta flights (GEVMLH) priced separately / already ticketed. Cruise fare not included in this total.

actionItems.action: Book Zone Transfers for Menorca (Mar 22): Mahón port → Subaida Farm (Alaior) → Mahón port. WhatsApp +34 654 381 547 (hours: 9:00–14:00 & 16:00–19:00), email info@zonetransfers.com.

Book excursion for Ponza (Mar 26) — arrange private boat circumnavigation. Contact: Cooperativa Barcaioli (+39 340 397 9916), ZioJack (+39 349 556 0424), or Ciccio Nero (+39 0771 80697). Or ask Four Seasons concierge.
Call Acqua Pazza (+39 0771 80643) to confirm open Mar 26 — off-season
Verify Erice cable car hours for March 27 (seasonal transition is March 28): funiviaerice.it
Contact Four Seasons concierge to arrange anniversary dinner onboard (Mar 27) — 22nd wedding anniversary, private table, champagne
Book ION Harbour by Simon Rogan for Sunday dinner in Valletta (Mar 29, 6:00–6:30 PM): +356 9911 0166. Best Sunday option — early dinner needed (4 AM airport departure).

shipInfo.question: What is the Four Seasons I?
shipInfo.answer: A 14-deck, 207-meter luxury yacht operated by Four Seasons Hotels and Resorts. Capacity of 222 guests in 95 suites. Launched in 2025 as one of the most exclusive cruise ships in the world.

shipInfo.question: What dining options are available onboard?
shipInfo.answer: Multiple restaurants including Terrasse (alfresco Mediterranean), Sedna (Japanese-inspired seafood), and additional venues. Breakfast at Terrasse (7:30–11:00 AM) is complimentary — the only included meal. All other onboard dining (lunch, dinner, room service) is pay-as-you-go. Reservations are made through the Four Seasons app or onboard concierge.

shipInfo.question: What is the dress code?
shipInfo.answer: Resort elegant. Think smart-casual for daytime; collared shirts and closed-toe shoes for evening dining. No formal night requirement, but many guests dress up for dinner. Swimwear is appropriate only at the pool deck.

shipInfo.question: Is Wi-Fi available?
shipInfo.answer: Complimentary high-speed Wi-Fi is available throughout the yacht, including in suites.

shipInfo.question: What about gratuities?
shipInfo.answer: Gratuities are included in the cruise fare. No additional tipping is expected, though it is welcomed for exceptional service.

shipInfo.question: What currency is used onboard?
shipInfo.answer: The onboard currency is USD. All purchases are charged to your suite account, which can be settled with a credit card.

shipInfo.question: What electrical outlets are in the suites?
shipInfo.answer: Suites have both European (Type C/F) and North American (Type A/B) outlets, plus USB-A and USB-C ports. No adapter needed for US devices.

shipInfo.question: What about shore excursions?
shipInfo.answer: Four Seasons offers curated excursions at each port, bookable through the app. Independent exploration is also welcome — the yacht's concierge can arrange private tours, cars, and restaurant reservations.

shipInfo.question: What is included in the cruise fare?
shipInfo.answer: Breakfast at Terrasse (7:30–11:00 AM daily), Wi-Fi, fitness center, non-motorized water sports, gratuities, and select excursions. All other dining (lunch, dinner, room service), beverages, spa treatments, specialty excursions, and premium experiences are additional fees.

shipInfo.question: How does tendering work?
shipInfo.answer: At some ports, the yacht anchors offshore and guests are ferried to shore via the yacht's own tender boats. The crew will announce tendering procedures each morning. Keep your cruise card with you at all times.
